title: Finite local coefficient models for restricted scalar-extension cohomology
statement:
Let $a:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and let $f:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Work on their small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with constant ring sheaves $A_T,B_T,A_X,B_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and the exact constant-coefficient inverse images $a_A^*,a_B^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and K-flat derived extension $K_B=K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}B_T$ with its right-factor $B_T$-action [def-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-scalar-extension, def-weil-derived-tensor]. Let $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ be bounded above. Suppose every $a_A^*\mathcal H^j(K)$ is locally constant and has finite geometric stalks [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. Then, for every $q\in\mathbf Z$, there is a pro-étale covering $\{V_{q,t}\to X\}_t$ and finite $B$-modules $M_{q,t}$ such that
$$\left(a_B^*\mathcal H^q(K_B)\right)|_{V_{q,t}}\simeq\underline{M_{q,t}}_{V_{q,t}}$$
as $B_X|_{V_{q,t}}$-module sheaves, using constant module sheaves on localized sites [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The covers may depend on $q$. No lower cohomological bound, constructible stratification, finite Tor amplitude, flatness of $B$ over $A$, or invertibility of a prime on $T$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a cochain representative $C^\bullet$ of $K$ and a K-flat resolution $P^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $L^\bullet=\operatorname{Res}_{A_T\to B_T}(B_T)[0]$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the complex $D^\bullet=P^\bullet\otimes_{A_T}B_T$, with right-factor $B_T$-action, represents $K_B$ in $D(B_T)$. After restricting scalars, this is exactly the tensor complex computing $K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}L^\bullet$ by [def-weil-derived-tensor]: forgetting the right-factor action does not change any term or differential [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); K-flat computation with the right-factor action

proof.text: Let $b$ be an upper cohomological bound for $K$. By [lem-pur-proetale-constant-module-pullback-homology], the termwise pullback of $C^\bullet$ has cohomology $a_A^*\mathcal H^j(K)$ and vanishes for $j>b$. The same lemma applies to $L^\bullet$, whose only possibly nonzero cohomology is the constant $A$-module sheaf with value $B$ in degree zero. Its pullback is the constant $A_X$-module with value $B$ by [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module]; the canonical coefficient identification for the actual pullback is [lem-pur-proetale-constant-coefficient-comparison]. This is locally constant and its geometric stalks are $B$, hence finite, by [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk]. The zero cohomology sheaves have zero constant models and finite zero stalks. Thus both inputs meet every bounded-above and local-constancy hypothesis of the restricted tensor lemma.

source.place: Tag 094H (lemma-locally-constant-tensor-product), input hypotheses; sites.tex Tags 0H7J and 00YV for constant-module inverse image

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-proetale-restricted-tensor-finite-local-constancy] with the scheme morphism $a$, the finite ring $A$, the complexes $C^\bullet,L^\bullet$, and the chosen acyclic-tensor K-flat resolution $P^\bullet\to C^\bullet$. Step 2 checks its upper bounds and the hypotheses for each nonzero input cohomology; for $C^\bullet$ these are precisely the hypotheses on $K$. For every $q$, its conclusion and the computation in step 1 give local constancy as an $A_X$-module and finite geometric stalks for $F_q=a_A^*\mathcal H^q(\operatorname{Res}D^\bullet)$.

source.place: Tags 094H (lemma-locally-constant-tensor-product) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), specialized to the second factor B_T[0]

proof.text: Write $E_q=a_B^*\mathcal H^q(K_B)$. We identify the underlying abelian sheaves of $E_q$ and $F_q$. Exact scalar restriction [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-derived-products] gives $\mathcal H^q(\operatorname{Res}D^\bullet)=\operatorname{Res}\mathcal H^q(D^\bullet)$: both are the kernel of the same differential modulo the image of the same preceding differential, with the action restricted. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], forgetting scalars from either the $A$- or the $B$-module inverse image gives $a^{-1}_{\operatorname{Ab}}$ of that same underlying abelian sheaf. These are the actual pullbacks used here because [lem-pur-proetale-constant-coefficient-comparison] makes both canonical maps $c_A^a,c_B^a$ invertible; tensoring along such an isomorphism merely identifies the coefficient ring. Together with step 1, this gives $|E_q|\simeq|F_q|$ as sheaves of sets. This comparison requires no flatness of $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi), underlying abelian inverse image; exact scalar restriction on kernels and images

proof.text: Choose a covering $\{U_t\to X\}$ and constant $A$-module models $N_t$ for $F_q$ by [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. If $U_t$ is nonempty, choose a geometric point $\bar u$ of it. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] the localized site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_t$ with ring $A_X|_{U_t}$ is identified with $(U_t)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with ring $A_{U_t}$, so the constant module sheaf of $N_t$ on the localized site is the constant module sheaf of $N_t$ on $(U_t)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (the same sheafification, transported along the identification of sites), and pointed neighbourhoods of $\bar u$ in the two sites correspond. The constant-module germ isomorphism [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk] on $(U_t)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ then identifies $N_t$ with the stalk there of $F_q|_{U_t}$, which is the stalk of $F_q$ at the composite point of $X$ and is finite by step 3. The restriction-stalk identification follows directly from [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]: pointed neighbourhoods admitting a map to $U_t$ are cofinal, since any pointed neighbourhood can be refined by its fibre product with $U_t$. On an empty $U_t$ replace the model by the zero module. Thus every $N_t$ can be taken finite. Pulling this cover back to any object of the site gives the objectwise finite locally constant set condition. Step 4 gives that condition for $|E_q|$ as well.

source.place: Definition 093Q (definition-locally-constant); finite local values from constant germs, with the empty covering member treated separately

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-finite-ring-action-local-constancy] on the chosen small pro-étale site of $X$, to the finite commutative ring $\Lambda=B$ and the $B_X$-module sheaf $E_q$. Step 5 supplies its hypothesis on the underlying set sheaf. Its conclusion, applied to the final object $X$, is a covering $\{V_{q,t}\to X\}_t$ and finite $B$-modules $M_{q,t}$ with $E_q|_{V_{q,t}}\simeq\underline{M_{q,t}}$ as module sheaves on the localized sites. This is the stated conclusion. The argument is for a fixed arbitrary $q$, so it imposes no common cover over all degrees and no lower cohomological bound.
